tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichl.summary: Tau Ceti has built most of this roadmap: `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/` holds 665 sorry-free declarations across 28 files, and Layers 0–4 are complete in the stated generality — the nonzero-ideal carrier with its zero extension, both completely multiplicative weight carriers with all constructors and the three rejection tests, `normCoeff` and `regroupByNorm`, ideal convolution with Möbius inversion and the von Mangoldt transform, `EulerProductData` with the analytic Euler product and a holomorphic branch of its logarithm, and the counting carriers with `primeTheta`, `primeCount` and `primePsi`. Layer 5 is complete but for the named density-zero corollary for degree-above-one primes, Layer 8 for the ordinary-versus-absolute abscissa equality (which no library can state, having no ordinary abscissa), and Layer 6 for the cancellation package `HasCancellation`/`continuedLFunctionOfWeight`; the arithmetic Perron formula that the roadmap's own STATUS.md calls untouched is in fact proved, as are the analytic Euler product, the log-derivative identity and the meromorphic Landau corollary. What is genuinely missing is a connected block: Wiener–Ikehara's final Tauberian step (the smoothed asymptotic is done, with only a crude `O(t log t)` growth bound derived; the Chebyshev bound and the passage to `x⁻¹ ∑_{n≤x} a n → κ` are not), the whole Dirichlet-density calculus of Layer 7 beyond the base Mathlib API the pinned revision already supplies, and consequently `PrimeBoundaryRemainder`, `primePsi_asymptotic_of_boundary` and the summit `primeNumberTheoremTransfer`. Mathlib contributes the ambient `LSeries`, `ArithmeticFunction`, `EulerProduct`, `AbelSummation` and `NumberField.Set.HasDirichletDensity` APIs but nothing ideal-indexed and no Tauberian theorem; its `NumberTheory/Chebyshev.lean` is the `K = ℚ` case of `primeTheta`/`primePsi`, of the higher-prime-power bound and of the ϑ-to-π Abel-summation identity.

AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli.summary: Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has an abelian scheme: the phrase does not occur in any Lean source in the baseline, and there is no base scheme, relative dimension, Picard functor, dual, polarization, Weil pairing, relative de Rham cohomology, Tate module, p-divisible group or Weil restriction anywhere. What exists is the field case and the linear-algebra shadow of the complex theory. Mathlib proves that a proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field is commutative (Stacks 0BFD) and that such a group scheme is smooth; Tau Ceti builds on those to define `AbelianVariety K` with dimension, zero section, base change along field extensions, products, hom groups, the endomorphism ring, isogenies and the tangent space at the identity, and separately has Cartier duality for finite locally free commutative affine group schemes — the one import A3 and A4 declare — together with a full polarized-Hodge-structure library that supplies the target category of A5's uniformization equivalence. Genuinely missing is almost everything the roadmap owns: the relative theory over a base, rigidity for pointed maps and the theorems of the square and cube, the Picard functor and the dual with Poincaré bundle and polarizations, torsion quotients and pairings, degree-one realizations and Serre–Tate, complex uniformization with the Siegel family, and the arithmetic Hom/End theorems with Weil restriction. A1 and A3 are the layers with real coverage, and only over a field: A1 through `AbelianVariety K`, A3 through its isogenies and through Tau Ceti's function-field theory of elliptic-curve isogenies, which proves `deg [n] = n²` and the separability criterion for `[n]`; A0 is an explicit import boundary and is process rather than mathematics.

targets.note: The layer states outright that it 'is an import boundary, not a second construction' and that its producer row 'imports exactly those general stages and reexports their hypotheses and universal properties'. It contains no mathematical target of its own, so it is bookkeeping. For the record the imported objects are themselves absent: neither library has algebraic spaces, a Picard functor or Picard scheme (the nearest object is Tau Ceti's `LineBundleClass X`, LineBundle/Class.lean:49, the monoid of isomorphism classes of line bundles on a scheme, still without inverses), a Hilbert functor, or Artin representability criteria.

AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.summary: Nothing this roadmap owns exists in either library. The decisive gap is at the very bottom: there is no étale fundamental group of a scheme anywhere in the baseline — Mathlib's `CategoryTheory/Galois/` develops Galois categories, fibre functors, Galois objects, prorepresentability and `IsFundamentalGroup` in the abstract, and `RingTheory/Etale/Finite.lean` has the category of finite étale algebras over a ring with its fibre functor at a geometric point, but the two are not joined, nothing covers a non-affine scheme, and the abstract theory is instantiated only for finite `G`-sets and, in Tau Ceti, for finite covering spaces of a space. Without it there are no path torsors, no Galois sections, no unipotent quotients and no Selmer varieties; independently, no declaration concerns Chabauty's method or Coleman integration (the two words occur only in Tau Ceti provenance comments), and `iteratedIntegral`, `NeronSeveri` and `anabelian` occur nowhere, and there is no p-adic height, no de Rham or rigid cohomology of a curve, no nonabelian `H¹`, and no Jacobian. The genuinely usable inputs are Mathlib's abstract Galois-category API, its finite étale algebras, low-degree abelian group cohomology and continuous cohomology (much extended in Tau Ceti), and Tau Ceti's Tannakian and unipotent-algebraic-group machinery, which would be the target category of NC.2. NC.6 is an export and conditionality-bookkeeping layer with no mathematics of its own.

targets.note: Mathlib has the abstract theory — Galois categories, fibre functors, Galois objects, prorepresentability, the equivalence with continuous finite `Aut F`-sets and the `IsFundamentalGroup` predicate — and, separately, the affine case of the fibre functor: `CommAlgCat.FiniteEtale R` is the category of finite étale `R`-algebras over any ring, `FiniteEtale.fiber R Ω` its fibre functor `S ↦ (S →ₐ[R] Ω)` at a geometric point, with base change and, over a separably closed field, the equivalence with finite sets (`equivOfIsSepClosed`). The two are not joined: no Galois-category instance is put on `FiniteEtale`, nothing covers a non-affine scheme (the phrase 'finite étale' does not occur in `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/`), and neither library defines an étale fundamental group of a scheme. The abstract theory is instantiated only for finite `G`-sets (Mathlib's `CategoryTheory/Galois/Examples.lean`) and, in Tau Ceti, for finite covering spaces of a topological space (`TauCeti.FiniteCoveringSpace.instGaloisCategory`, TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Classification/GaloisCategory.lean:329), the topological analogue, not the arithmetic one.

ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights.summary: The general height theory this roadmap needs as input is already in Mathlib, and more generally than the roadmap assumes: `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Height/` defines `AdmissibleAbsValues` — a family of absolute values satisfying the product formula with archimedean multiplicities — proves the product formula for every number field, builds multiplicative and logarithmic heights on tuples and on projectivizations, and proves Northcott finiteness for elements of a number field (`finite_setOfPred_mulHeight₁_le`, `finite_setOfPred_logHeight₁_le`) together with an abstract `Northcott` order class; Northcott for points of projective space is still a TODO there. Everything the roadmap actually owns is absent: `Arakelov`, `Faltings`, `Zarhin`, `arithmeticDegree`, `hermitianBundle` and `NeronModel` each have zero occurrences in the whole baseline, and the geometric inputs are missing too — there is no abelian scheme, no Néron or semistable model, no module of invariant differentials, no period lattice attached to a curve and no polarized moduli scheme. So no hermitian bundle, no arithmetic degree, no Hodge bundle with Faltings metric, no (stable) Faltings height, no isogeny formula and no theta-height comparison exists. The roadmap's own summary anticipates this correctly when it says general heights and Northcott 'are necessary but do not construct the stable Faltings height'; the audit's addition is that most of the necessary part is finished in Mathlib: the product formula and elementwise Northcott should simply be consumed rather than built, while Northcott on projective space is still missing.

ArithmeticDynamics.summary: The libraries supply most of this roadmap's two general inputs and almost nothing else. Mathlib's `Mathlib/Dynamics/PeriodicPts/` gives iteration, fixed and periodic points, minimal period, periodic orbits and the divisibility calculus for an arbitrary self-map (but no preperiodic points) — more general than DY.0's morphisms of varieties, and at the level of maps rather than sampled points — and `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Height/` gives admissible absolute values with the product formula, logarithmic heights, elementwise Northcott finiteness over number fields, and the bound `h(F x) = N h(x) + O(1)` for a morphism of projective space given by homogeneous forms. On top of those Tau Ceti has, for elliptic curves over any field with admissible absolute values, the complete Néron–Tate package DY.1 asks for in its abelian-variety acceptance example: the Tate limit with its convergence proved, the bounded difference from the naive height, the exact functional equation `ĥ(2P) = 4ĥ(P)`, quadraticity, and the theorem that canonical height zero is equivalent to torsion via Northcott. Everything else is missing, and mostly missing at the level of vocabulary: `Berkovich`, `dynatomic`, `equidistribution`, `arboreal`, `MordellLang` and `Lattès` each have zero occurrences in the whole baseline, and there is no self-map of `P¹` given by coprime forms, no dynamical degree or resultant of such a pair, no polarized morphism, no ample line bundle, no local height and no metrized line bundle. DY.1's general polarized construction, and DY.2–DY.6 entirely, are unbuilt; the sharpest overlap in the atlas is `GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.1`, which states DY.1's canonical-height targets for abelian varieties almost word for word.

targets.target: iteration of a self-map, orbit maps, periodic and preperiodic points
targets.note: Mathlib's `Mathlib/Dynamics/PeriodicPts/` develops iteration, `IsFixedPt`, `IsPeriodicPt`, `periodicPts`, minimal period, the periodic orbit as a `Cycle` and the whole divisibility calculus for an arbitrary self-map of a type, which covers the periodic half of this target in greater generality than a morphism of varieties. Because it is stated for `f : α → α` and `f^[n]`, an equality of iterates really is an equality of maps, satisfying the layer's acceptance criterion. Preperiodic points are not defined — the word occurs in neither library, although `∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ periodicPts f` is one line — and there is no forward-orbit map of a self-map (Mathlib's orbits are for flows and group actions). The scheme-theoretic layer is absent as well: iteration of a morphism of varieties as a morphism, and orbit maps as morphisms.

targets.target: conjugacy of maps under automorphisms
targets.note: Mathlib has semiconjugacy of self-maps and transport of periodic points along it, which is the set-level statement; the dynamical notion of two rational maps being conjugate by an automorphism of `P¹`, and the invariants of that conjugacy class, are absent.

targets.target: rational functions on `P¹` given by coprime homogeneous forms, with degree, resultant and good reduction
targets.note: The resultant of two univariate polynomials exists in Mathlib with a Tau Ceti extension (Sylvester matrix, behaviour under `AdjoinRoot`, discriminant). There is no self-map of `P¹` presented by a pair of coprime homogeneous forms, no dynamical degree, no resultant of such a pair, and no dynamical good reduction; `HasGoodReduction` exists only for a Weierstrass curve at a prime. The required worked example — a map whose displayed resultant vanishes at a bad prime — has no carrier.

targets.target: for `f*L ≅ L^d` with `L` ample and `d > 1`, the canonical height as the limit `d^(-n) h_L(f^n P)`
targets.note: The Tate limiting construction is done in Tau Ceti for the doubling map on an elliptic curve over any field with `[Height.AdmissibleAbsValues F]` — so over any number field, not only ℚ. `canonicalHeight P = ½ lim h(2^n P)/4^n`, and the limit is proved to be attained, so the value is not `limUnder`'s junk value. The general polarized statement (arbitrary `f`, ample `L`, `f*L ≅ L^d`) is absent, because there is no ample line bundle, no `h_L`, and no polarized morphism in either library. For `ℙⁿ` with `L = O(1)` the height-machine input of Tate's argument is in Mathlib: for a family of homogeneous forms of degree `N`, `Height.logHeight_eval_le` gives `h(F x) ≤ N h(x) + C`, and `Height.logHeight_eval_ge` gives `h(F x) ≥ N h(x) − C` when the forms have no common zero, witnessed by a Nullstellensatz-type certificate; nothing applies them to iterates or builds the limit.

targets.target: the error bound `|ĥ - h| ≤ C`, the functional equation `ĥ(f P) = d · ĥ(P)`, and uniqueness
targets.note: The error bound and the functional equation are proved in the elliptic case: `canonicalHeight_two_nsmul` is `ĥ(2P) = 4 ĥ(P)`, the exact `d = 4` functional equation, and the parallelogram law upgrades it to full quadraticity with `ĥ(n • P) = n² ĥ(P)`. Uniqueness among bounded-error refinements is *not* stated as a named theorem in either library; it is used implicitly inside the limit argument (`tendsto_nhds_unique` at CanonicalHeight.lean:246) rather than exported.

review.notes: Reviewed all 147 targets of the five roadmaps. Mechanical check: the audit's 258 citations (238 distinct declarations in 70 files) all resolve in the pinned declarations.tsv at the claimed library, file and line; no cited file contains a sorry token (at this pin Tau Ceti has sorry and axiom only inside comments); nothing cited is an axiom, and the cited structures and classes are carriers, not proofs. Three cited names were aliases deprecated on 2026-07-09 and are replaced by their targets. Statements: every cited declaration was read against its target. The five built verdicts (ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layers 0–4) were confirmed target by target, and both process verdicts (A0, NC.6) match their layer text. Absences: essentially every absent or partial claim was searched again by concept and by Mathlib naming convention, over the index and both source trees. Substantive errors found and fixed: (1) the Wiener–Ikehara entry and the summary said the Chebyshev growth bound is derived, but only O(t log t) is, which the source file itself calls one logarithm short of Chebyshev; (2) AbelianSchemes A3's [n] target was marked absent, although Tau Ceti proves deg [n] = n², the separability criterion for [n] and #ker [n] = n² for elliptic curves over a field, so the target is partial and A3 is now partly built, and the claim that no isogeny has a degree was wrong; (3) ArithmeticDynamics DY.0 put periodic and preperiodic points wholly in Mathlib, but preperiodic points are defined in neither library; (4) Arakelov R35.6 said Northcott is done in the generality needed, including tuples, but Mathlib has it only for elements and lists projective Northcott as a TODO; (5) NC.3 said there is no continuous cohomology of a Galois group, but Mathlib defines continuous cohomology and Tau Ceti builds the Kummer map into H¹(G_K, μₙ) on it. Several 'zero occurrences' claims (Siegel, Chabauty, Coleman, semistable, Pic of a scheme) were literally false and are reworded; their substance stands. Missed inputs now cited include Mathlib's finite étale algebras with their fibre functor (NC.0), Mathlib's Chebyshev file (ADS), the polynomial-map height bounds h(F x) = N h(x) + O(1) (DY.1), the Weierstrass ℘ equation (A5), Tau Ceti's fppf quotient sheaf and elliptic isogeny degree (A3, R35.4), its Tannakian reconstruction theorem (NC.2) and the Galois action on roots (DY.5). Duplicates: all 58 original claims resolve to live atlas stages, none in the retired FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration, and each is borne out by the target stage's text (NC.2 → R06.5 and NC.3 → R02.6 are declared-supplier links, and their notes say so); 11 were added, for 69 in all. 47 corrections in all; after them there are 281 citations, each checked at its exact file and line and sorry-free.
